To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the exocytotic coupling in mouse pancreatic β cell is similar with that in rat pancreatic β cell.
the exocytotic process in pancreatic β cells is regulated by three pools of vesicles, namely an immediately, a readily releasurable, and a reserve releasable vesicle pool.

the exocytosis of mouse pancreatic β cell is coupled to the influx of extracellular Ca2+ through voltage-gated L-type channels, which are activated by a depolarizing pulse, or a flash of UV light, and the release of Ca2+ from internal stores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Ca2+-dependent secretion in mouse pancreatic β cell.
the characteristics of the exocytosis of mouse pancreatic β cell.
the Ca2+-stimulate exocytosis coupling mechanism in isolated mouse pancreatic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exocytosis of insulin in mouse β cells is triggered by Ca2+ influx through voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels and is mediated by a complex process of Ca2+ signals.
the Ca2+ current in mouse pancreatic β cell is not sufficient to induce the exocytosis.
the Ca2+-exo-cytosis coupling in mouse pancreatic β cell was similar to that in the other cell types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exocytosis of mouse pancreatic β cell is Ca2+ dependent, and the Ca2+ signal is a major determinant in exocytosis.
the exocytosis of mouse pancreatic β cell is a complex process, which involves multiple pools of vesicles, and the Ca2+-dependent vesicle fusion process is a highly regulated one.
the Ca2+ current in β cells is small, and the Ca2+ signal is not sufficient to trigger exocytosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exocytotic process in mouse pancreatic β cell is more complex than that in rat pancreatic β cell, and the exocytosis of mouse β cell is more sensitive to the Ca2+ signals.
the readily releasable pools are more likely the major source of exocytosis, which may be due to the higher Ca2+ sensitivity of this pool.
the readily releasable and reserve pools are distinct pools of vesicles that are not simply different sizes of the same pool.
